item.title: Xi: Development, security key to SCO
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
Xi: Development, security key to SCO SCO: Leaders encourage greater role in peace, stability President Xi Jinping called on Tuesday for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization to prioritize development and security to usher in a future of shared prosperity and foster an environment of universal security. Xi made the remarks when addressing the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the SCO, which was held in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. He underlined the need for the SCO to remain committed to dialogue and consultation for more equitable and orderly governance. In his speech, Xi hailed the extraordinary journey of the regional organization over the past 25 years, saying that it has grown into a new type of regional cooperation grouping with the largest land area and population and enormous development potential. Founded in 2001 by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, the SCO now comprises 10 member states, two observer states and 15 dialogue partners. Xi said that the most valuable spiritual asset of the regional grouping is that it pioneered, and has since invariably followed, the Shanghai Spirit featuring mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for the diversity of civilizations and pursuit of common development. Its most important cooperation experience is that it has found the right way of coexistence, featuring nonalliance, nonconfrontation and not targeting any third party, enabling countries in the region to build a common home together, he added. As the world is undergoing accelerated changes unseen in a century, with the intensifying rivalry between dialogue and confrontation, win-win and zero-sum, and multilateralism and unilateralism, Xi urged the SCO to step forward to shoulder its historical responsibility and proactively steer the course for the future. He also called for the SCO to advocate universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, solidify cooperation in traditional fields such as trade, investment, mutual connectivity, energy and resources, and expand cooperation in emerging fields like artificial intelligence, digital economy, green industry and green mining in order to deepen and upgrade regional cooperation. China sees the SCO as a priority area for promoting high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and implementing the Global Development Initiative, he said. In 2025, China's trade with other SCO members reached $523.5 billion and accounted for 8 percent of the country's total foreign trade, up from $12.1 billion in 2001, according to statistics from the Ministry of Commerce. Xi urged the SCO countries to take coordinated measures to tackle traditional and nontraditional security threats, and he called for efforts to prevent external forces from interfering in their internal affairs, endangering their political security and undermining regional stability. China is willing to work with all parties to practice a common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security concept and make the SCO an important platform for implementing the Global Security Initiative, he added. Xi also emphasized the need for the SCO countries to uphold a people-centered approach and cement the foundation for everlasting friendship. China stands ready to work with all parties to implement the Global Civilization Initiative, he added. The summit was chaired by President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan, which holds the current rotating presidency of the SCO. The leaders of the SCO member states fully affirmed the development achievements of the SCO over the past 25 years, recognizing that the SCO provides important guarantees for regional security and prosperity and has become one of the cornerstones of global stability and economic development. They praised China's significant contributions as a founding member state in promoting the organization's development and agreed to actively implement the strategic blueprint from the SCO Tianjin Summit in 2025. In the face of a complex international situation, SCO member states should work together to enhance the organization's influence, promote the building of a more just and reasonable global governance system, and play a greater role in safeguarding the peace, stability and prosperity of the region and the world, they said. Leaders of the SCO member states signed and issued the Bishkek Declaration on the 25th Anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, approved the Protocol on Amending and Supplementing the Charter of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, the Regulations on the SCO Universal Center for Countering Security Challenges and Threats, and the Regulations on the SCO Anti-Drug Center, and adopted 28 outcome documents covering security, economic, people-to-people and cultural cooperation, as well as organizational development. It was decided at the summit that Pakistan will assume the rotating presidency of the SCO for 2026-27. Li Ziguo, director and research fellow in the Department for European-Central Asian Studies at the China Institute of International Studies, said the summit could give fresh impetus to implementing the outcomes of last year's summit and help move the SCO into a stage of pursuing development in tandem. Sun Zhuangzhi, director of the Institute of Russian, Eastern European and Central Asian Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, described China's efforts in practicing the Shanghai Spirit as an important driving force behind the SCO. Zhao Jia contributed to this story.

item.title: Sino-Egyptian mission unveils key relics in Memphis
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
A joint archaeological team from China and Egypt has uncovered a number of important relics and artifacts near Cairo, the Egyptian capital, shedding new light on the site's historical features and human activities across different periods. The results of the archaeological mission at the Sekhmet Temple site in the ancient city of Memphis, about 20 kilometers south of Cairo, were announced on Tuesday at the Shanghai Museum. The joint excavation was conducted by archaeologists from the museum and Egypt's Supreme Council of Antiquities. The temple site in Memphis was discovered in 1959, according to Xinhua News Agency, and it witnessed archaeological missions in 1961 and 1962. Chen Jie, deputy director of the Shanghai Museum, said that the joint team completed the first large-scale systematic excavation of the site and its surroundings in more than six decades. "It was our first excavation mission to Egypt, so we wanted to choose a site that we Chinese scholars consider important," he said. The city of Memphis was built around 3100 BC, and it served as the capital of ancient Egypt during the Old Kingdom (2686-2181 BC) period. The Sekhmet Temple, located in the core area of Memphis, was part of the Great Temple of Ptah complex, which was dedicated to the Egyptian god of creation. Chen said that the joint excavation work, which was carried out from October to June, has revealed new details about the Sekhmet Temple's structure, its reuse later, and the everyday life that continued around it for centuries. The team started preliminary fieldwork by clearing most of the aboveground remains of the temple, revealing its basic layout and internal structure. The rectangular temple was mainly built of limestone, with some stone components bearing ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs, providing important clues for determining the temple's purpose. Archaeologists also uncovered the remains of a mud-brick residential area nearby, consisting of multiple houses and courtyards. They found a large number of stone architectural components and statue fragments in later layers that disturbed the original structures. On the east side of the temple, the team found a limestone structure. As grape seeds were discovered at its base, the structure was preliminarily identified as a facility that may have been used for wine production. Large quantities of discarded faience fragments also suggest that the area may have once contained a craft workshop. These findings suggest the reuse of the temple and its surroundings, demonstrating long-term continuous human activity in the settlement. "We've adopted some new technical methods, documenting and registering all of our archaeological data, which have been recognized by our Egyptian colleagues," Chen said. "In next year's excavation, we plan to invite more experts to help us to carry out deeper research into the connections between environmental evolution and urban settlement evolution." Mohamed Abdel-Badie, head of the Egyptian Antiquities Sector at Egypt's Supreme Council of Antiquities, said that even after the Sekhmet Temple declined as a major religious center, life in ancient Memphis continued, with the city gradually transforming into a residential area. The Shanghai Museum said it hopes to display the findings of the archaeological mission in an exhibition at its upcoming north branch.

item.title: Peng welcomes Kyrgyz performers to visit China
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
Peng welcomes Kyrgyz performers to visit China In order to give Chinese audiences a closer look at Kyrgyzstan's rich ethnic culture, Peng Liyuan, wife of President Xi Jinping, extended welcome on Tuesday to Kyrgyz artists to visit China for more performances and cultural exchanges. Peng made the remarks while watching a stage performance at the Enesay Reception House with spouses of other leaders attending the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit 2026 in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. She noted that the performance was wonderful and praised the performers for their outstanding artistry. The show was part of the activities organized on Tuesday morning by Aigul Japarova, wife of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov, for spouses of relevant leaders. Upon her arrival at the Ala-Archa State Residence, Peng was warmly greeted by Japarova. Peng and the others also viewed an exhibition on the ethnic culture of Kyrgyzstan and posed for group photos. zhoujin@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: President calls for closer friendship with Egypt
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
President calls for closer friendship with Egypt President Xi Jinping arrived in Egypt on Tuesday, setting foot in the land nourished by the Nile for the second time. Upon arrival at Cairo International Airport, Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, were warmly welcomed by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife, Entissar El-Sisi. "Once you drink from the Nile, you are destined to return," Xi invoked an Egyptian proverb in a signed article published by Egyptian media outlets on Tuesday. "During my last visit 10 years ago, I was deeply impressed by the time-honored, profound civilization of this country, together with its booming vitality and upward momentum," Xi wrote. Xi said he looks forward to renewing his friendship and working together with President El-Sisi to explore ways of cooperation and map out a new blueprint for deepening the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership. The visit comes as China and Egypt mark the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties. For seven decades, the China-Egypt relationship has braved wind and rain, and withstood the test of a changing international landscape, staying on the right course, remaining robust as ever, and sustaining a strong momentum, Xi said. The relationship is a fine example of China's cooperation with Arab states and Africa, and for friendship, solidarity and collaboration between developing nations, he added. Xi noted that both countries are at a critical stage of development and revitalization. China saw its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) get off to a good start, and is striving to open up new ground in Chinese modernization. Egypt is making vigorous efforts in building the New Republic and forging ahead toward its Vision 2030. "The Chinese side is ready to work with the Egyptian side to deepen the comprehensive strategic partnership, advance building of a community with a shared future, and join hands in realizing modernization," Xi wrote. He called on the two sides to keep supporting each other on core interests and major concerns, and deepen exchanges and cooperation at various levels and across sectors to ensure the baton of friendship is passed on from generation to generation. Xi urged the two countries to forge more synergy in development strategies, engage in high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, proactively tap the potential and expand the scope of pragmatic collaboration in a bid to provide sustained impetus to the mutually beneficial cooperation. Xi called on both China and Egypt to "take pride in who we are while setting an example for exchanges and mutual learning". The two sides should deepen exchanges and cooperation in education, tourism, science and technology, health, sports and archaeology, Xi said. Such efforts would forge a stronger bond of understanding and affinity, with a view to injecting new momentum into the comprehensive strategic partnership, and harnessing the strengths of diverse civilizations to promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi added. He underscored the shared responsibilities of China and Egypt in upholding fairness and justice as major developing countries and important members of the Global South. With profound changes unfolding in a volatile international landscape, China and Egypt should uphold world peace and stability, and international fairness and justice by practicing true multilateralism, enhancing multilateral coordination and working together to deliver on the four global initiatives, he said. Xi called on the two countries to join hands to lead the way in China-Arab and China-Africa cooperation. Egypt plays an important role in promoting cooperation between China and Arab states, and between China and African countries, he said. The Chinese side is ready to work with the Egyptian side to enhance the demonstration effect of their cooperation, Xi said. "For 70 years, China and Egypt have stood by each other rain or shine. Now our two countries are embarking on a new journey with enterprise and fortitude," he wrote. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Equal, orderly multipolar world urged
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
Equal, orderly multipolar world urged President Xi Jinping called on Tuesday for joint efforts to advance an equal and orderly multipolar world and make global governance more just and equitable, saying that Global South countries should have greater representation and a stronger voice in international affairs. Xi made the remarks at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Plus Meeting in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, which focused on strengthening the role of the United Nations and building a multipolar world. Against the backdrop of accelerating changes unseen in a century, Xi said that hegemonism, unilateralism and protectionism are resurging against historical trends. Nevertheless, the overwhelming majority of the world does not condone power politics, conflict and confrontation, or isolation and backwardness, he said, adding that what most people want instead is to hold a place on the world stage through national development and international cooperation. Noting that the rise of the Global South is driving a profound shift in the international balance of power, Xi said that the trend toward a multipolar world is irreversible. "As a responsible major country, China advocates for an equal and orderly multipolar world," he said. The Chinese president identified sovereign equality and mutual respect as fundamental principles, balance, order and the rule of law as inherent requirements, multilateralism, dialogue and consultation as essential pathways, and mutual benefit, win-win cooperation and inclusiveness as the way forward for development. "We should ensure equal rights, equal opportunities and equal rules for all countries, regardless of their size, strength and wealth," Xi said. The common values of humanity should be upheld, while double standards, exceptionalism, foreign interference, bullying and the law of the jungle should be rejected, he said. He added that major countries, in particular, should "take the lead in observing international norms and honoring the rule of law", and work together to tackle global challenges. "World affairs should be discussed by all, and international norms should be set by all. The authority and vitality of the UN need to be restored," Xi said. He also called for focusing on the development agenda, upholding openness and cooperation, and bridging the digital and artificial intelligence divides, so that the technological revolution and development achievements can benefit all nations. Xi said that after a 25-year journey, the SCO has successfully set a stellar example in conducting relations among big countries, among neighbors and among countries of different sizes. To advance common prosperity in the vast region straddling Asia and Europe, Xi called for harnessing "SCO Strength" and connecting multiple growth poles across the continent through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. Xi also called on the SCO to promote the development and rise of the Global South through "SCO Wisdom", urging all sides to carry forward the Shanghai Spirit and strengthen and expand the SCO Plus partnerships. He said that "SCO Action" should guide the reform and improvement of global governance. Tuesday's meeting came exactly one year after Xi proposed the Global Governance Initiative at the SCO Plus Meeting in Tianjin. The initiative has since received support from nearly 160 countries and international organizations, while more than 60 countries have joined the Group of Friends of Global Governance. Li Yonghui, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of Russian, Eastern European and Central Asian Studies, said that the rise of the Global South and emerging economies is accelerating the shift toward a multipolar world. Li said that the SCO provides a practical example of cooperation among countries with different social systems and at different stages of development. zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: CXMT surging forward in memory race
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
CXMT surging forward in memory race Chinese chipmaker's DRAM to debut in Xiaomi's upcoming foldable Chinese memory-chip maker ChangXin Memory Technologies is moving closer to a vanguard position amid the global DRAM race with one of the earliest commercial deployments of LPDDR6 in a flagship smartphone, industry experts said on Monday. They made the comments as CXMT said on Saturday that it had begun mass production of its self-developed LPDDR6 DRAM, which will debut in Xiaomi's upcoming 18 Fold handset. The chip has a peak data-transfer rate of 12,800 megabits per second and capacity of up to 16 gigabytes. "For a Chinese company that only began mass-producing its first DRAM products in 2019, the bigger significance is not simply being first with one product," said Wang Peng, a researcher at the Beijing Academy of Social Sciences. "It put CXMT into the first wave of competition around the latest mobile-memory standard alongside global heavyweights Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology," Wang said. LPDDR6 is designed to raise memory bandwidth and parallelism while cutting power consumption, with these features becoming increasingly important as artificial intelligence models migrate from cloud data centers into phones, PCs, cars and other modalities. The Xiaomi partnership adds another dimension. It puts a Chinese-designed mobile processor and the country's newest-generation DRAM together inside a premium smartphone. Xiaomi founder and CEO Lei Jun said the company's Xring O3 would support CXMT's LPDDR6, and he expects deeper collaboration among Chinese tech companies. Advanced chips require years of engineering but also large-scale customer validation to improve yields, reliability and costs. China's huge base of smartphone, computer, electric vehicle and internet companies can give local chipmakers something laboratory breakthroughs alone cannot provide — millions of devices on which new technology can be tested and refined, industry experts said. Liu Zhiying, a professor at the University of Science and Technology of China, said, "An important factor in the growth of Chinese high-tech companies is their ability to connect research, commercialization and market applications, allowing leading companies to pull suppliers across the industrial chain forward." CXMT's technological progress is arriving alongside a dramatic expansion in its financial firepower. On Monday, shares of CXMT closed at 58.01 yuan ($8.6), down 1.01 percent on the day, valuing the company at about 3.94 trillion yuan and making it one of China's most valuable listed companies. The company recently reported first-half revenue of 150.31 billion yuan, up about 874 percent from a year earlier, while net profit attributable to shareholders reached 77.61 billion yuan, reversing a 2.33 billion yuan loss a year earlier. The surge was driven by sharply higher memory prices and rising sales as demand for computing power tightened global DRAM supplies, the company said. CXMT has grown into the world's fourth-largest DRAM producer, behind Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron, turning China from a marginal player in memory chips into an increasingly consequential competitor. Last week, CXMT sued the US Department of Defense in federal court in Washington, seeking removal from a Pentagon list of companies alleged to have ties to China's military. CXMT said its chips are designed primarily for civilian and commercial use and that it has no affiliation with the Chinese military. It said the designation was unsupported by facts and had damaged its reputation and business interests since it was first placed on the Pentagon's blacklist in January 2025. The lawsuit follows similar legal challenges by Chinese companies including Xiaomi and WuXi AppTec. Xiaomi successfully challenged an earlier Pentagon military designation in 2021. Zhang Sinan, an independent commentator who has been following the situation, said, "The US can keep extending the list, but the world will not stop needing cheaper clean energy, more efficient electric vehicles, more advanced drug development services or more flexible robotic applications simply because of a list." chengyu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: For villagers, life continues in temporary shelter
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
For villagers, life continues in temporary shelter Around 8 am on Monday, Kelsang Palmo began packing luggage for her son, who was about to start junior high school in the Gyirong county seat, about 70 kilometers away. She stuffed a backpack with homemade Tibetan flatbread, apples, packaged cakes, cold medication and a thermos, along with a suitcase containing winter clothing and other daily necessities. After a mudslide struck Gyirong Port in the Xizang autonomous region on Wednesday morning, Kelsang Palmo and her family from Kopa village, near the hardest-hit border crossing, were relocated to a hotel to avoid secondary disasters. Despite the disruption caused by the mudslide, authorities have tried to maintain a sense of normalcy for local villagers, allowing the rituals and rhythms of daily life to continue. Kelsang Palmo's son was among five children staying at the hotel who were picked up by an arranged vehicle around noon on Monday and taken to junior high school. Throughout the morning, doors were left open as neighbors popped in and out of rooms, offering khata — silk scarves traditionally presented when welcoming or seeing off guests — to the children. "In our tradition, each household also gives departing students some pocket money — maybe 5 to 10 yuan ($0.74 to $1.48) — as a blessing, and also so that they have some change to buy snacks while away from home," said Karma, head of Kopa village. The temporary shelter at the hotel provides free accommodation, including three meals a day, as well as medical care and psychological support, for about 120 relocated residents from Kopa and Trungsi villages. "We also have a group of volunteers helping address their needs. These past few days, some have accompanied parents who are not familiar with this area to nearby stores to purchase items such as winter jackets for their children," Karma said. As relocated villagers are unable to tend to their cattle, chickens or crops at home, several officials have also remained in the village to help with poultry and farm work. "They stay in facilities that have passed safety inspections, and we are constantly monitoring local environmental conditions to ensure their safety as well," Karma said. Butri and her brother, Migmar, were both excited to start the new semester. "I really like the free meals provided here, especially the white rice," Migmar said. "But I am also looking forward to visiting the school because I've never been there." Butri said she was keen to meet her new classmates and kick shuttlecock with them. While life continues, traces of the disaster remain visible. The thumping of helicopters flying overhead can be heard constantly at the hotel. Residents have also put their favorite pastime of dancing and singing on hold out of respect for those who lost their lives in the mudslide. Sangmo, mother of the siblings, occasionally scrolled through video clips of the mudslide sweeping down the area. She did not see the waves of mud and ice herself, but she remembers hearing a deafening sound at the time. "It was horrifying," she said. "Our life here is nice, but I also miss my home." Contact the writers at wangxiaoyu@chinadaily.com.cn

The 2026 SCO Summit was held in Bishkek, the capital of the Kyrgyz Republic, from Aug 31 to Sept 1. In a recent interview with China Daily, Djoomart Otorbaev, former prime minister of the Kyrgyz Republic, said that connectivity goes far beyond roads and railways, embracing broader and multidimensional links; pragmatism enables cooperation among countries with different systems and national conditions into real results; and autonomy empowers the Global South to pursue independent development and shape its own future. item.title: A bridge between Chinese and Arab cultures
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-01
A bridge between Chinese and Arab cultures Share - WeChat
With ties between China and Arab countries growing ever closer, language is playing an increasingly important role in connecting people and creating new opportunities. In Shishi, Fujian province, a free Arabic language program is helping Chinese merchants overcome language barriers and expand their reach into Arab markets. Across the Arab world, growing access to Chinese language education is opening new pathways to education, employment and deeper cultural exchange. Language is building bridges, turning dialogue into understanding and connections into lasting friendships.
